**Page:** 2017‑18 Harassment or Bullying Civil Rights Data Collection – http://catalog.data.gov/dataset/2017-18-harassment-or-bullying-civil-rights-data-collection  

**Evidence**  
- Title & Year: *“2017‑18 Harassment or Bullying Civil Rights Data Collection”*【source】.  
- Publisher: Office for Civil Rights (OCR) | Department of Education【source】.

  * “On basis of disability – reported” – XLSX – download URL: https://civilrightsdata.ed.gov/assets/downloads/2017-2018/School-Climate/Harassment-or-Bullying/Harassment-Bullying-on-basis-of-disability_reported.xlsx【source】.

**Coverage**  
- **Entity:** All U.S. states (explicitly stated “for all states”).  
- **Condition:** Students reported as harassed or bullied (not disciplined) **on the basis of race** (i.e., race‑related harassment or bullying).  
- **Measurement:** Count of reported students.  
- **Unit:** Number of students (integer count).  
- **Date/Timeframe:** 2017‑18 U.S. school year (implied by the dataset title and description).  
- **Scope:** Full set of states; all three spreadsheets per file (total, male, female) are available in the downloaded Excel files.  

**Missing**  
- State‑specific counts of reported race‑based harassment/bullying students for the 2017‑18 school year.  
- Counts of full‑time equivalent (FTE) school counselors for each state for the same year.  
- Computed ratio of counselors to students for each state.  
- Identification of which of South Carolina, North Carolina, Georgia, or Virginia has the highest such ratio.

- (Similarly, for counselor data a separate dataset would be needed – not present on this page.)  

**Expand:** yes – downloading the “on basis of race – reported” XLSX will supply the missing state‑level student counts needed to compute the counselor‑to‑student ratio.

# 2017-18 State and National Tables

This set of Excel files contains data for all states on overall enrollment, enrollment of students served under IDEA, enrollment of students served under Section 504, and enrollment of students who are English language learners. For each category, there are three spreadsheets: total students, male students, and female students.
